title: Registration data can be linked to an existing identity
description: The authentication service receives a strong identifier set during parent registration, including email, full name, government ID, and a six-digit code. These attributes can be correlated with existing records or external datasets, allowing the newly created account and future activity to be linked to the same individual across contexts.
assumptions: The service stores or can access prior records keyed by email, government ID, or similar identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether linkage is modeled via stored identifiers or cross-context correlation.

title: Parent identity can be directly identified from registration attributes
description: The flow contains direct identifiers and highly identifying data, notably email, name, and government ID. Anyone with access to this flow or the receiving process can directly identify the parent user.
assumptions: The registration payload is accessible to the receiving process, logs, intermediaries, or administrators beyond the data subject.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for direct identifiability from explicit identifiers.

title: Sensitive registration data may be disclosed in transit or at receipt
description: The registration flow carries sensitive personal data and credentials, including password and government ID. If transport protection, endpoint hardening, or secure handling are insufficient, these data may be exposed to unauthorized parties through interception, logging, debugging traces, or improper access at the authentication service.
assumptions: There is some possibility of interception, verbose logging, or unauthorized internal access.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of data in transit/processing; exact subtree may differ by whether the focus is network interception, endpoint exposure, or logging.

title: Excessive collection during registration enables unnecessary data disclosure risk
description: Collecting government ID together with email, name, password, and a six-digit code at initial registration may exceed what is strictly necessary for account creation. Over-collection increases privacy risk because more personal data are exposed if the flow, logs, or backend are compromised.
assumptions: Government ID is not strictly required at this stage, or less intrusive alternatives exist.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping for data minimization/non-compliance versus disclosure differs across versions.

title: Parent may be unaware of why government ID and code are required
description: If the registration interface or process does not clearly explain the purpose, retention, and use of the government ID and six-digit code, the parent user may not understand what data are being collected and why. This undermines transparency and informed participation.
assumptions: The flow description does not indicate that clear notices or just-in-time explanations are provided.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency; exact subtree may vary by whether notice, purpose explanation, or consent context is emphasized.

title: Registration may violate data minimization or lawful-basis requirements
description: Processing government ID and other registration data without a clearly justified purpose, lawful basis, retention limit, or proportionality assessment may create non-compliance risk under privacy regulations. The combination of direct identifiers and credentials heightens the compliance impact.
assumptions: Applicable privacy obligations require necessity, proportionality, purpose limitation, and protection of special identifier handling.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance; exact subtree depends on the specific compliance obligation being modeled.

title: Parent may be unable to prove or dispute submitted registration details
description: If the authentication service does not provide reliable evidence of what registration data were submitted, when, and under what notice or consent context, the parent user may later be unable to repudiate false submissions or the service may be unable to resolve disputes about what was provided.
assumptions: The system may lack tamper-evident records, confirmation receipts, or auditable submission metadata.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this flow than other threats; node id is a best-fit estimate.

title: Stored parent account record may reveal identity
description: Storing a parent account in the users collection can directly expose identifying attributes such as name, email address, phone number, username, or persistent account identifiers to anyone with access to the datastore or backups.
assumptions: The parent account record contains direct identifiers or unique account identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for identity disclosure may vary.

title: Parent account entries may be linkable across services or events
description: A persistent parent account stored in MongoDB can enable linking of the same individual across sessions, child accounts, devices, or other backend datasets through stable identifiers, email addresses, or internal account keys.
assumptions: The stored record includes stable identifiers reused across contexts or datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability may differ.

title: Stored account data may disclose sensitive personal details
description: The parent account record may contain personal data beyond identifiers, such as contact details, relationship to a child, authentication metadata, or profile attributes. Unauthorized access to the datastore would disclose these details.
assumptions: The parent account schema includes personal or account-related attributes beyond a bare identifier.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for information disclosure may vary.

title: Storing parent account without adequate purpose limitation or minimization
description: If the authentication service stores more parent-account data than necessary, or stores it without a clear lawful basis, retention limit, or transparent purpose, the flow may violate privacy obligations and internal policy requirements.
assumptions: The system may collect or retain attributes not strictly necessary for authentication/account management.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; non-compliance node mapping is approximate without the project's specific LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Users may be unaware that parent account data is persisted in MongoDB
description: Parents may not understand what account attributes are stored, for how long, and for which downstream uses, reducing transparency and informed expectations about processing.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-product explanations may be incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact detectability/awareness subtree may differ.

title: Presence of a stored parent account may allow detecting whether a person is registered
description: If access patterns, error handling, or indirect exposure of the users collection reveal whether a parent account record exists, an attacker or unauthorized party could detect whether a specific individual is registered as a parent.
assumptions: Some interface, query path, or side channel can reveal record existence.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact detectability subtree may vary.

title: Excessive disclosure of user attributes in authentication response
description: The authentication service sends a JWT plus user data to the parent user. If the response includes more profile attributes or claims than are necessary for the parent-facing use case, personal data may be disclosed unnecessarily to the recipient or exposed through downstream storage, screenshots, browser caches, or logs.
assumptions: The flow may include profile fields beyond the minimum needed to establish the session or identify the child/account context.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for attribute/data over-disclosure, but exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: JWT enables cross-context linkability of the parent
description: If the JWT contains stable identifiers, account IDs, email addresses, or reusable subject claims, the parent user can be linked across sessions, services, devices, or relying parties that observe or process the token or copied claims.
assumptions: The JWT may contain persistent identifiers or claims reused across contexts rather than pairwise/pseudonymous identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via persistent identifiers in tokens; exact node id may differ in a specific LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Readable JWT payload reveals personal data to unintended observers
description: JWTs are often only signed, not encrypted. Any party with access to the token in transit endpoints, browser storage, logs, crash reports, or support tooling may read embedded claims and associated user data, disclosing personal information.
assumptions: The JWT is a JWS or otherwise readable by the recipient and potentially by intermediaries or local software; transport/storage protections may be imperfect.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for disclosure through readable token contents.

title: Parent may be unable to prove or contest receipt of specific user data
description: If the system does not maintain privacy-respecting evidence of what JWT and user data were delivered to the parent, the parent may later be unable to demonstrate that certain personal data was received, or may be unable to repudiate receipt if the service claims it was delivered.
assumptions: Delivery/audit records may be incomplete, ambiguous, or retained without user-accessible evidence.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this flow than disclosure/linkability; node id is approximate.

title: Parent may be unaware of which personal data and claims are contained in the JWT
description: Because token contents and derived user data are often opaque to end users, the parent may not understand what personal information is being transmitted, how long it remains valid, or which parties can inspect and reuse it.
assumptions: The interface does not clearly explain token contents, recipients, retention, or reuse implications.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for insufficient transparency/unawareness; exact node id may vary.

title: Authentication response may violate data minimization or purpose limitation
description: Sending JWT plus user data to the parent may exceed what is necessary for authentication alone, potentially conflicting with privacy requirements such as data minimization, purpose limitation, or storage limitation if the parent-facing client stores or reuses the data.
assumptions: The flow is intended primarily to establish authentication/session state, and additional user data is not strictly necessary for that purpose.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because non-compliance mappings differ across LINDDUN Pro variants.

title: Authentication service can identify the child via parent email used as login credential
description: The login flow requires submission of a parent email together with a password. The authentication service can directly identify or single out the child account by linking the supplied parent email to a specific family or household record, enabling identity association during each login attempt.
assumptions: The parent email is stored as an account identifier or is otherwise mapped to the child user's account.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for direct identification through credentials; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Repeated logins using the same parent email enable linkability of the child's sessions
description: Using a stable parent email as part of login allows the authentication service, and potentially connected logging or analytics components, to link multiple authentication attempts and sessions to the same child or household over time.
assumptions: The same parent email is reused across sessions and login events are logged or otherwise observable within the service.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for linkability via persistent identifiers; exact numbering may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Login credentials disclose personal data about the child-parent relationship
description: The parent email submitted during child login reveals personal information beyond mere authentication data, including the existence of a parent account and an association between the child user and a specific parent or household. This may disclose more personal data than necessary for the child's authentication event.
assumptions: The parent email is personally identifying and its use implies a relationship to the child account.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for exposure of personal data in transit/processing; exact subtree id may vary.

title: Authentication attempts may disclose credentials or identifiers through logs or error handling
description: If the authentication service logs incoming login requests, debugging data, or verbose authentication errors, the parent email and possibly password-related information may be exposed to operators or ancillary systems, increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: Request parameters, failed login attempts, or error traces may be logged or surfaced to support personnel or monitoring systems.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because this threat depends on implementation details such as logging and error-message practices.

title: Child may be unable to plausibly deny a login attempt tied to the parent email
description: Because login attempts are associated with a stable parent email and likely recorded by the authentication service, the service can later attribute a specific authentication event to that child account or household, reducing the child's ability to deny having initiated the action.
assumptions: Authentication events are logged with timestamps and account identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-repudiation/privacy threat node; exact numbering may differ by LINDDUN Pro release.

title: Using parent email for child login may exceed data minimization or valid-consent expectations
description: Requiring a parent email as the child's login identifier may process more personal data than necessary for authentication and may create compliance concerns around children's privacy, parental data use, and transparency if users are not clearly informed or given a less intrusive alternative.
assumptions: A less identifying child-specific credential could be feasible, and applicable privacy requirements impose minimization/transparency obligations for children's data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because non-compliance mappings vary across LINDDUN Pro catalogs and depend on jurisdiction and system context.

title: Exposure of child status and profile data to unintended recipients on the client side
description: The flow delivers a JWT explicitly indicating userType=child together with child profiles to the Child User endpoint. If the token or profile payload is exposed through insecure client storage, browser history, logs, screenshots, shared devices, or interception at the recipient side, sensitive information about a minor and their profile data may be disclosed to unintended parties.
assumptions: Assumes the child uses a client device or app where tokens/profile data may be stored, rendered, or cached.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id chosen as a generic information disclosure node; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether the catalog distinguishes transfer, display, storage, or interception disclosure.

title: JWT enables linkability of child sessions and actions
description: If the JWT contains stable identifiers, persistent subject claims, or other unique attributes, the child's sessions and actions across time or across relying components can be linked together. Combining the token with child profile data increases the chance of correlating activity to the same child account.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT includes stable claims such as subject identifiers, account ids, or long-lived metadata reused across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit generic linkability node; exact subtree depends on whether the token contains direct identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or correlatable metadata.

title: Over-disclosure of child profile attributes
description: Sending child profiles together with authentication material may disclose more personal data than is necessary for the immediate authentication response. Excess profile fields such as age, preferences, guardianship-related metadata, or internal identifiers increase privacy exposure for a minor.
assumptions: Assumes the full or broad child profile is returned rather than a minimized subset strictly needed by the recipient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for excessive attribute disclosure; exact node naming in LINDDUN Pro may differ.

title: JWT and profile data may identify the child directly or indirectly
description: The JWT and returned child profiles may contain direct identifiers or combinations of attributes that uniquely identify the child. Even if names are omitted, persistent account identifiers or distinctive profile combinations can make the child identifiable.
assumptions: Assumes token claims or profile fields include direct identifiers or sufficiently unique combinations of attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic identifiability node; exact subtree depends on whether identification is direct, indirect, or via combination with auxiliary data.

title: Processing of child data may lack valid consent or age-appropriate transparency
description: Returning a JWT marked as child and associated child profiles implies processing personal data of a minor. If this occurs without verifiable parental authorization where required, without age-appropriate notices, or beyond the purposes communicated to the child/guardian, the flow may violate privacy obligations and consent requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to child-data protection obligations and that consent/notice/purpose controls may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic non-compliance node; exact node id may differ depending on whether the issue is consent, transparency, purpose limitation, or data minimization non-compliance.

title: Child may be unaware that profile data is bundled with authentication response
description: The child user may reasonably expect only an authentication token, but the flow also returns child profiles. If the interface does not clearly explain what profile data is sent, why it is needed, and how it will be used or retained, the data processing may be insufficiently transparent to the child.
assumptions: Assumes the UI or service does not clearly communicate the bundled data transfer in child-appropriate language.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic unawareness node; exact subtree may depend on whether the concern is hidden collection, hidden transfer, or unclear purposes.

title: Collection of directly identifying child data
description: The flow sends highly identifying attributes for a child profile—name, date of birth, gender, and government ID—to Child Profile Management. This enables direct identification of the child and creates privacy risk if the data is not strictly necessary or is over-collected for profile creation.
assumptions: Assumes the child can be uniquely identified from the submitted attributes and that all listed fields are stored or otherwise processed by P3.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a best-fit for identifiability via direct identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro node labeling may vary.

title: Linkability of child profile to other records via government ID and demographics
description: Government ID combined with name, date of birth, and gender can link the child profile to records in other systems or future interactions, allowing correlation across contexts that may not be expected by the parent or child.
assumptions: Assumes the government ID or demographic combination is stable enough to correlate records across systems or sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability through stable identifiers; exact node id may differ in some LINDDUN Pro catalogs.

title: Disclosure of sensitive child identity data in transit
description: The flow carries sensitive personal data about a child, including government ID and date of birth. If the transmission channel is not adequately protected, an attacker or unintended recipient could intercept or observe the data.
assumptions: Assumes there is some possibility of network exposure, logging, or routing through components not fully trusted.
uncertainty_note: Node selected as a generic disclosure/interception-in-transit threat; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary.

title: Disclosure through excessive logging or storage at profile management
description: Child Profile Management may log request payloads or persist raw onboarding data, exposing name, DOB, gender, and government ID to administrators, support staff, backups, or downstream systems beyond what is necessary.
assumptions: Assumes application, API gateway, or audit logs may capture full request contents.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure due to internal storage/logging; exact node id may differ.

title: Non-compliant collection of child personal data without adequate legal basis or parental consent handling
description: Creating a child profile using name, DOB, gender, and government ID may violate child-data protection requirements if the system lacks appropriate legal basis, parental authorization checks, age-related safeguards, data minimization, or retention controls.
assumptions: Assumes the service is subject to privacy regulations governing children's data and identity documents.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance in collection/processing of regulated child data; exact node id may vary.

title: Insufficient transparency about why government ID and child attributes are required
description: The parent may not understand why each attribute—especially government ID—is needed for child profile creation, how it will be used, who can access it, and how long it will be retained, undermining user awareness and informed decision-making.
assumptions: Assumes the interface or notice accompanying the flow may not clearly explain purpose, necessity, and retention.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of user awareness/transparency; exact node id may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of parental submission and consent choices
description: If the system does not record what the parent submitted, when, and under which consent or notice terms, the parent or operator may later be unable to prove or dispute the creation of the child profile and the associated privacy choices.
assumptions: Assumes profile creation may require demonstrating parental action or consent state later.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation/accountability gaps around submission and consent evidence; exact node id may vary.

title: Unauthorized modification of child profile data before storage
description: The child profile management process may update or overwrite profile attributes in ways not authorized by the child, parent, or policy, causing incorrect or excessive personal data to be stored in the childprofiles collection.
assumptions: P3 accepts profile update inputs and writes them to DS2; authorization and field-level validation may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for integrity/unauthorized modification; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Excessive disclosure of stored child profile data
description: If the childprofiles collection stores more profile attributes than necessary, or stores sensitive child data in clear form, later access to the datastore can reveal personal information beyond what is needed for the service purpose.
assumptions: DS2 contains personal data about children, potentially including sensitive attributes, and may be accessible to internal components or administrators.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit generic disclosure node; exact subtree depends on the LINDDUN Pro catalog version.

title: Linkability of child records across updates and contexts
description: Persisting stable identifiers and rich profile attributes in the childprofiles collection can allow multiple updates and related records to be linked to the same child over time, enabling profiling or correlation across contexts.
assumptions: Profiles use persistent child identifiers or quasi-identifiers and are retained across multiple transactions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic linkability node; exact node numbering may differ by threat-tree edition.

title: Loss of data quality or provenance for child profile updates
description: The datastore may not preserve who changed which child profile fields and when, making it difficult to verify the correctness and source of stored personal data and increasing the risk of inaccurate child profiles being used.
assumptions: DS2 may not maintain immutable version history or provenance metadata for profile changes.
uncertainty_note: This is framed as integrity/provenance risk; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Repudiation of child profile changes
description: Without reliable audit trails for writes to the childprofiles collection, a user, parent, administrator, or service component could deny having created or modified a child profile, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant changes.
assumptions: Write operations from P3 to DS2 may not be strongly logged with actor identity, timestamp, and change details.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic non-repudiation threat node; exact subtree may vary.

title: Insufficient transparency about profile storage and updates
description: Data subjects or guardians may be unaware that child profile data is being stored, updated, retained, or enriched in the childprofiles collection, limiting their ability to understand processing and exercise privacy rights.
assumptions: The system may not provide clear notices, dashboards, or change visibility for stored child profile data.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness often maps to notice/transparency-related nodes; exact node id may differ.

title: Storage of child profile data beyond consent or legal basis
description: The child profile management process may store or update child profile attributes without verifying parental consent, age-related requirements, purpose limitation, or another valid legal basis, resulting in non-compliant processing.
assumptions: This flow handles children's personal data and compliance obligations may require consent checks, minimization, retention limits, and purpose restrictions before writing to DS2.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic non-compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Search, like, and comment actions can be linked to the same child user
description: Repeated video searches, requests, likes, and comments sent from the child user to the service can be correlated over time and tied to the same account, device, IP address, or session, enabling construction of a behavioral profile.
assumptions: The service can observe persistent identifiers such as account ID, cookie, device ID, IP address, or authenticated session.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability of multiple actions on one flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Video interaction data can identify the child user
description: Search terms, requested videos, likes, and especially free-text comments may directly or indirectly reveal the identity of the child user when combined with account data or contextual metadata.
assumptions: The service stores or can access account/profile data and metadata associated with the incoming requests.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability from content and metadata; exact subtree may differ.

title: Sensitive interests and traits may be disclosed from viewing and interaction history
description: The flow reveals what videos a child searches for or requests and what they like or comment on, which can expose preferences, habits, emotional state, education level, health-related interests, religion, politics, or other sensitive attributes.
assumptions: The service logs or analyzes search, request, like, and comment events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for inference/disclosure of personal information from interaction history.

title: Insufficient transparency about collection and use of child interaction data
description: The child user may not understand that searches, requests, likes, and comments are collected, retained, profiled, or shared for recommendations, moderation, analytics, or advertising-related purposes.
assumptions: Notices are absent, unclear, overly complex, or not age-appropriate for children.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/disclosure-related node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may vary.

title: Secondary use of child activity data beyond the expected video interaction purpose
description: Interaction data submitted for searching, requesting, liking, or commenting may be reused for profiling, personalization, experimentation, moderation training, or third-party analytics in ways not expected by the child user.
assumptions: The service uses the data for additional internal or external purposes beyond fulfilling the immediate request.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for policy/consent non-compliance or unexpected processing; exact subtree id may differ.

title: Processing of child user data may violate children's privacy requirements
description: Collecting and processing a child's searches, viewing requests, likes, and comments without valid parental authorization, age-appropriate notices, data minimization, or lawful basis may breach child-specific privacy obligations.
assumptions: The user is a child and the service is subject to child privacy and data protection requirements.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree id may vary by catalog version.

title: The service may be unable to prove valid consent or authorization for child interactions
description: If the service cannot demonstrate that appropriate consent, parental authorization, or policy acceptance was obtained for collecting comments, likes, and search history, it may be unable to resolve disputes about whether processing was permitted.
assumptions: The service relies on consent/authorization but lacks robust records, timestamps, or audit trails.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit repudiation-related node focused on inability to prove actions/permissions; exact subtree id may differ.

title: Excessive video metadata stored enables identification of uploader or subjects
description: When the Video Management Service stores video metadata in MongoDB, fields such as uploader account identifiers, device identifiers, IP-derived location, timestamps, or embedded EXIF-like attributes can directly or indirectly identify individuals associated with the video.
assumptions: The metadata schema may include user, device, location, or capture-context attributes beyond what is strictly necessary for core video management.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for storing directly/indirectly identifying data; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree naming may vary.

title: Cross-record linkage through persistent video and uploader identifiers
description: Persisting stable video IDs together with uploader IDs, channel IDs, tags, timestamps, and engagement-related metadata in the collection can allow records to be linked across uploads, sessions, or other datasets, revealing behavioral patterns about creators or data subjects appearing in videos.
assumptions: Records are retained with stable identifiers and may be queryable or exportable together with rich metadata.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers and correlated attributes.

title: Sensitive video metadata or file references may disclose personal information
description: Stored metadata and references to video files may reveal personal information such as titles, descriptions, thumbnails, categories, geolocation, participant names, or storage paths/URLs. If accessed beyond intended purposes, this can disclose information about uploaders or people depicted in the videos.
assumptions: The collection stores descriptive metadata and possibly pointers to underlying media objects that themselves contain personal data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for information disclosure from stored content; exact subtree may differ.

title: Over-retention of video metadata and file references enables detectability over time
description: If the service stores metadata and file references longer than necessary, the continued presence of records makes it possible to detect that a person uploaded, appeared in, or was associated with a video at a later time, even after the original purpose has expired.
assumptions: Retention periods may be undefined, long, or not aligned with user expectations and deletion policies.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability caused by persistent storage/retention; exact node id may vary.

title: Users may be unaware that rich metadata and file associations are stored
description: The flow may store more than the obvious video content, including derived metadata, technical attributes, moderation status, or storage references. If this is not transparent to users, they may not understand what personal data is being processed and retained.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-product explanations may not fully describe all stored metadata elements and retention behavior.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency regarding data storage.

title: Storage of video metadata and files may exceed consent or stated purpose
description: The service may store metadata fields, derived attributes, or file associations that are not necessary for the stated purpose of video management, or retain them for secondary purposes such as analytics, moderation history, or profiling without an appropriate legal basis or valid consent.
assumptions: Processing purposes may expand beyond core upload and retrieval, and consent/legal basis may not cover all stored attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance due to purpose limitation, data minimization, or legal-basis issues.

title: Insufficient evidence of user-approved storage or deletion actions
description: If the collection stores video records without reliable provenance, timestamps, or audit attributes tied to user actions and policy decisions, the system may be unable to demonstrate whether a user requested upload, update, or deletion of a video and its metadata.
assumptions: Auditability and provenance for create/update/delete operations may be incomplete or stored separately.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation due to missing evidence around data handling events.

title: Search and watch history can be linked to a specific child profile
description: When Child Profile Management stores search and watch history in the childprofiles collection, the records are likely associated with a persistent child profile identifier. This enables linking multiple viewing and search events over time to the same child, creating a detailed behavioral profile.
assumptions: The stored history includes a stable child profile ID or equivalent account/profile reference.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Stored history may identify a child directly or indirectly
description: Search and watch history stored in the childprofiles collection may reveal the identity of a specific child directly through profile metadata or indirectly through unique combinations of watched content, search terms, timestamps, and household context.
assumptions: The datastore contains profile metadata and/or sufficiently granular history records.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for identifiability from stored attributes and behavioral traces.

title: Behavioral history discloses sensitive interests and habits
description: A child's search and watch history can disclose personal interests, routines, preferences, developmental traits, or potentially sensitive topics. If accessed beyond the intended purpose, the stored data exposes private behavioral information about the child.
assumptions: History entries are retained with enough detail to infer interests or habits.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed approximation for information disclosure from stored content.

title: History retention enables excessive profiling over time
description: Persistently storing search and watch history in the childprofiles collection may retain more personal data than necessary and for longer than needed. This increases the risk of building long-term profiles of a child and using the data beyond the original service context.
assumptions: Retention limits, minimization, or aggregation are absent or weak.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node choice for data minimization/retention concerns; exact subtree numbering may differ.

title: Secondary use of child history may exceed user expectations
description: Search and watch history collected to support profile functionality may later be used for recommendations, analytics, personalization, parental reporting, or marketing-related purposes without clear alignment to the original expectation at collection time.
assumptions: The stored history is accessible to other internal functions or downstream processing.
uncertainty_note: Best estimate for an unawareness threat related to unclear or unexpected downstream use.

title: Storing child behavioral history may violate consent or child-data rules
description: Persisting a child's search and watch history may require specific consent, parental authorization, purpose limitation, retention controls, and heightened protections for children's data. If these conditions are not met, the storage operation may be non-compliant with applicable privacy obligations.
assumptions: The system processes personal data of children in a regulated context.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate; this is a general non-compliance threat grounded in child-data handling obligations.

title: Video upload reveals parent identity to the service
description: The uploaded video and associated submission metadata can directly identify the parent user to the Video Management Service, especially if the account, contact details, child context, or visible faces/voices are attached to the submission.
assumptions: The upload is associated with a parent account or submission record rather than being fully anonymous.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on general LINDDUN Pro knowledge; exact subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Uploaded video can be linked to other submissions or accounts
description: The Video Management Service may link this uploaded video and its approval/rejection event with the same parent's other uploads, account activity, device identifiers, or child records, enabling profiling across interactions.
assumptions: The service stores persistent identifiers, account references, or metadata that allow correlation across events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on general LINDDUN Pro knowledge; exact subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Approval or rejection decision discloses sensitive information about the parent or child

description: If the system does not provide a durable receipt, timestamp, content hash, or decision rationale, the parent may be unable to demonstrate what was uploaded, when it was submitted, or challenge an incorrect approval/rejection outcome.

title: Video upload and moderation may occur without valid consent or appropriate legal basis
description: Because uploaded videos can contain personal data of the parent, child, and possibly bystanders, processing for upload handling and approval/rejection may be non-compliant if consent, parental authority, child protections, or another legal basis is inadequate.

description: If the approved video stream or associated metadata is delivered over an insecure or improperly scoped channel, network observers or other unauthorized parties could learn which video the child is watching, revealing preferences or behavioral information.

description: The specific video delivered, timing of delivery, or visible restrictions may reveal that the service maintains approval status, age-related rules, or behavioral inferences about the child, disclosing internal personal-data processing to the child or nearby observers.
